target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox exec-server subprocesses (both the process RPC path and the streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream `error` events, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox child process exits or its pipes break, the Node stream layer emits `error` on the child's stdout/stderr `Readable` streams. With no `error` listener attached, Node re-throws the event, which bubbles into a process-fatal unhandled error and terminates the exec-server bridge. Both subprocess owners — `processes.ts` (process RPC) and `http.ts` (streaming HTTP) — had this gap.

The fix attaches a no-op `error` listener on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` at each spawn point, mirroring the repo-standard pattern already used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The process `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle and finalization.

Rebased onto current `main`; resolved a conflict with #103617 (defer sandbox cleanup until process close), which restructured both spawn sites into a `try/catch`. The no-op listeners are now attached after the guarded spawn, preserving that ownership.

## User Impact

The Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess output pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**Production change (both subprocess owners):** after the guarded `spawn`, before the `data` listeners, each spawn site attaches no-op `error` listeners on `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` (`processes.ts`, `http.ts`), mirroring `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`. The `close` handler stays authoritative for lifecycle/finalization.

**Real integration proof — executes the patched code outside Vitest over a real WebSocket bridge.** A standalone `tsx` harness imports and calls the real exported entry points — `startProcess()` → `runProcess()` (process-RPC owner) and `httpRequest({streamResponse:true})` → `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest()` (HTTP owner) — over a real `ws` bridge. Only the sandbox backend seam is stubbed; the `spawn`, stdout/stderr listeners, close lifecycle, JSON-RPC notifications, and ws bridge are all real. No `spawn` module mock, no Vitest.

Process-RPC owner — real `runProcess`, real streaming child, induced real stdout/stderr pipe error; the bridge survives and stays usable:

```text
[host] real bridge streamed 10 process/output notifications over the ws
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] bridge still usable after error: readProcess ok (chunks=10, exited=true)
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] child close after the error emitted process/closed = true
[host] PASS: real patched runProcess survived the induced pipe error; bridge stayed OPEN
```

Negative control on the same real path — removing the fix's real stdout error listener from the live child reproduces the pre-fix crash, proving the listener is load-bearing:

```text
[host] stripped the fix's real stdout error listener (pre-fix state)
[host] inducing a real stdout/stderr pipe error on the real child ...
[host] UNCAUGHT EPIPE: induced sandbox stdout pipe failure -> exec-server bridge host crashed
[shell] exit=1
```

HTTP owner — real `runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest` executes end-to-end with the same guards attached:

```text
[host] real httpRequest(streaming) executed end-to-end: status=200, bodyDeltas=1
[host] ws bridge socket.readyState = 1 (1=OPEN)
[host] PASS: real patched runStreamingSandboxHttpRequest executed over the real bridge with the stdout/stderr guards attached
```

<details>
<summary>Proof integration harness (executes the real exec-server entry points; backend seam stubbed, spawn/streams/bridge real)</summary>

```ts
import { WebSocket, WebSocketServer } from "ws";
import { startProcess, readProcess, terminateProcess } from "./sandbox-exec-server/processes.js";
import { httpRequest } from "./sandbox-exec-server/http.js";

let hostCrashed = false;
process.on("uncaughtException", (e) => {
  hostCrashed = true;
  console.log(`[host] UNCAUGHT ${e.message} -> exec-server bridge host crashed`);
  process.exit(1);
});

async function socketPair() {
  const wss = new WebSocketServer({ host: "127.0.0.1", port: 0 });
  await new Promise((r) => wss.once("listening", r));
  const client = new WebSocket(`ws://127.0.0.1:${wss.address().port}`);
  const server = await new Promise((res) => wss.once("connection", res));
  await new Promise((r) => client.once("open", r));
  return { wss, client, server };
}

// Stub ONLY the backend seam; buildExecSpec spawns a REAL child.
const makeExecServer = (argv) => ({
  sandbox: {
    containerWorkdir: "/tmp",
    backend: {
      buildExecSpec: async () => ({ argv, env: process.env, finalizeToken: "tok" }),
      finalizeExec: async () => {},
    },
  },
});

// mode "process-survive": run real startProcess, induce a real stdout/stderr error, assert bridge OPEN.
// mode "process-strip":   same, but managed.child.stdout.removeAllListeners("error") first -> host crashes.
// mode "http-execute":    run real httpRequest({streamResponse:true}) end-to-end over the real ws bridge.
// (full runnable harness kept in the contributor outputs)
```

</details>

**Mutation-sensitive regression test** (`sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts`): captures the real spawned child and emits `error` on the real `child.stdout`/`child.stderr` for both the process RPC and streaming HTTP paths, asserting each stream carries an `error` listener, that emitting the error does not throw, that the WebSocket bridge stays `OPEN`, and (process path) that the bridge still runs follow-up work. Removing either production listener makes the test fail.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

The same no-op `error` listener pattern already ships in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

```text
$ cd /tmp/openclaw-proof-101777 && cat stream-error-lifecycle.txt

=== proof: http stream-error lifecycle ===

  ws connected, readyState=1
  http/request sent (child alive, no headers)
  child pid=2714157 alive=true
  stdout EPIPE emitted
  request rejected: sandbox http/request output stream error: EPIPE: broken pipe
  ws readyState=1
  finalizeExec calls before close: 0
  finalizeExec: {"status":"failed","exitCode":1,"timedOut":false}
  finalizeExec calls after close: 1

=== summary ===
  settled               = YES
  ws survived            = YES
  no finalize before close = YES
  finalize after close   = YES
```

The induced stream-error proof confirms: (1) request settles with error before headers, (2) WebSocket bridge stays OPEN, (3) finalizeExec is NOT called before child close — the lease is held for the full process lifetime, and (4) finalizeExec is called exactly once after close with status=failed.

**ClawSweeper P1 repair:** the streaming HTTP pre-close failure paths now settle the request once, send `SIGTERM` to the one-shot helper when needed, and leave backend `finalizeExec` owned by the child `close` handler. The proof child intentionally ignores `SIGTERM`, which proves the request is settled and termination is requested while `finalizeExec` remains at zero until the child is force-closed; after close, `finalizeExec` is called exactly once with `status: "failed"`.

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx .tmp-proof-101777.ts
stream-error rejected=true
stream-error message=sandbox http/request output stream error: EPIPE: induced stdout failure
stream-error socketOpenBeforeClose=true
stream-error finalizeBeforeClose=0
stream-error finalizeAfterClose=1
stream-error finalizeStatus={"status":"failed","exitCode":1,"timedOut":false,"token":"stream-error-token"}
malformed rejected=true
malformed socketOpenBeforeClose=true
malformed finalizeBeforeClose=0
malformed finalizeAfterClose=1
malformed finalizeStatus={"status":"failed","exitCode":1,"timedOut":false,"token":"malformed-token"}
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

ClawSweeper's requested focused sandbox exec-server suite also passes on the repaired head:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.http.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.lifecycle.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

CI follow-up after the latest rebase: the streaming HTTP response reader and output-stream error helpers were extracted out of the oversized `http.ts` file, and the branch now passes the TypeScript LOC ratchet locally.

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/check-ts-max-loc.ts --base "$(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)"
TypeScript LOC ratchet: checked 4 changed production files.
```
